Tells the host to adjust game graphics settings for the selected stream resolution and FPS.
Helps video recovery after lost or corrupted packets by invalidating unusable reference frames.
Treats the connection as a remote/WAN stream. Use this for Internet or routed connections; leave it off for a normal local LAN.
Waits for the Vita display VBlank when presenting video frames. This can reduce tearing, but may affect latency and frame pacing.
Limits presentation to the selected FPS by dropping excess decoded frames when they arrive too quickly.
Keeps game audio on the PC instead of streaming audio to the Vita.

Video: resolution, codec, target FPS and video payload bitrate (Mbps). FPS: received, decoded and submitted to PAF; PAF is not the physical display rate. RTT/variation: round-trip network delay and its fluctuation (ms). Drops: frames missing before decoding, skipped by the pacer or replaced in the PAF queue (%). Decode call/PAF queue: average decoder call time and queue wait (ms). Host min/max/avg: PC processing time (ms), when available. Video stalled: no recent frames. Unavailable measurements are hidden.
When the video aspect ratio does not match the Vita screen, shows the center portion instead of fitting the entire image. Edges may be cropped.
Enables diagnostic messages in psp2shell. No log file is written.
Sends the Vita gyroscope and accelerometer data to the PC as motion input.
Enables sprinting by quickly double-tapping the forward movement control.
Maximum time between the two taps for double-tap sprint, in milliseconds.
Swaps the functions of R1/L1 with R2/L2.
Controls how much touch or analog mouse movement is accelerated. Higher values make the cursor move farther.
Captures the Vita PS button during streaming. A double press opens the menu; a single press can be sent to the host as a PS/Xbox button.
Enables predefined front-screen touch zones for special keys. Touches in active zones are used as those keys instead of normal touch input.
Selects how the Vita front touchscreen is presented to the host: off, DS4-style touchpad, absolute mouse, or Sunshine tablet mode.
Enables the custom controller mapping configuration used by Moonlight.
Sets how much of this back-touchscreen edge is reserved as a deadzone. Higher values move the active area farther inward.
